findings.title: Disabled or removed selected carry can block departure with no usable clear action
trigger: Unlock and select the sole affordable Home item.
A designer disables appearance_weight/home_enabled or removes its current definition while the profile keeps selected_home_item.
Formal startup rejects can_select=false. Disabled existing tile displays cancel but disables it; removed definition has no row at all.
No global clear-selection action exists, so without another selectable item the player cannot depart.
evidence: App refuses selected IDs unavailable in current policy before Home teardown.
Action availability and _request_item both reject available=false, including cancellation.
Backend already permits home_select empty ID without requiring current catalog entry.
findings.recommended_fix: Provide an always-available explicit no-carry/clear-selection intent when selection is nonempty; retain owner, focus, generation and revision validation. Cancellation must work for missing/disabled selected definitions.
findings.original_status: P2 confirmed by static production trigger chain; reported to root before repair
findings.resolution: Current UI adds always-visible CodexClearSelection whose eligibility depends only on nonempty selected ID, plus chosen-item cancellation before source availability check. App still validates Home/focus/pause/revision/context. This makes disabled and missing selected entries cancellable without a replacement purchase.

findings.title: Unlock submits a freshly computed quote instead of the displayed quote
trigger: Open a discovered locked item showing price5 with enough notes.
Update config/home_items.json to price25 without changing the profile revision; old UI remains displayed.
Press the old unlock action. App validates the unchanged revision, computes current price25/fingerprint, and passes that current fingerprint to backend.
Backend accepts and debits25 although displayed quote was5.
evidence: UI signal carries ID and profile_revision only.
Backend quote fingerprint correctly covers definition/policy bytes/revision/price, but caller supplies new fingerprint at submit time.
findings.recommended_fix: Bind current displayed rows/quote fingerprints to the Home codex session and submit that captured fingerprint, rejecting policy/catalog changes with stale_quote before any debit.
findings.original_status: P2 confirmed by static production trigger chain; reported to root before repair
findings.resolution: App caches every displayed row.quote_fingerprint at _refresh_home_codex and passes the captured fingerprint on unlock. Current backend recomputes canonical quote and rejects stale_quote before debit; App maps refusal to explicit no-charge message.

findings.title: Pending discovery retries are not bound to the originating profile owner
trigger: A committed acquisition in profileA fails permanent saving and remains in _pending_item_discoveries.
Reconfigure the exposed MetaProgression owner to profileB or replace App.meta before retry (candidate startup already replaces meta).
Any _refresh_home_meta calls _flush_item_discoveries, which writes pending A item IDs into current metaB.
evidence: Pending entries store item_id only; key contains run/event, no captured owner/profile/slot epoch.
MetaProgression correctly resets its own in-memory data on profile switch, but does not own App pending entries.
No profile identity comparison precedes retry.
findings.scope_note: Current shipped Home menu exposes one local profile; multi-slot UI is not claimed. This affects the new profile-aware owner API and App replacement boundary, so prevent cross-owner retry before adding slot UI.
findings.recommended_fix: Bind queued discovery to the originating MetaProgression/profile identity/owner epoch; retry only the matching owner, never another profile. Preserve failed records for their original owner rather than dropping them silently.
findings.original_status: P2 confirmed by static production trigger chain; reported to root before repair
findings.resolution: MetaProgression.profile_context_id combines owner instance ID and incrementing configure epoch. App captures it for the current view, checks it before submit, and queues each pending discovery with its context. Retry erases mismatched contexts instead of writing another profile.

production_snippets.view_submit:
func _request_item(id: StringName, selecting: bool, generation: int, revision: int, detail_generation: int) -> void:
	if not _view_current(generation) or _submitted or revision != _profile_revision or detail_generation != _detail_generation or id != _focused_id or not _rows.has(id): return
	var row: Dictionary = _rows[id]
	# Clearing an existing choice is valid even after its catalog entry was
	# disabled; the global action also handles a completely removed definition.
	if selecting and id == _selected_id:
		_request_clear(generation,revision)
		return
	if not bool(row.get("discovered",false)) or not bool(row.get("available",false)): return
	if selecting != bool(row.get("unlocked",false)): return
	if not selecting and _notes < maxi(0,int(row.get("price",0))): return
	_submitted = true
	if is_instance_valid(_action): _action.disabled = true
	if is_instance_valid(_clear_button): _clear_button.disabled = true
	if selecting:
		requested_select.emit(&"" if id == _selected_id else id,revision)
	else:
		requested_unlock.emit(id,revision)
